solves: Lets the person pick a value, or a range, on a continuous scale of numbers, by dragging a thumb or with the arrow keys, and takes part in the form that contains it.
use_when: single, to pick an approximate value on a scale, such as volume or brightness.
range, to filter by a range, such as a minimum and a maximum price.
vertical, in a narrow panel or for a setting that goes up and down, such as volume or zoom.
text, outside nph-field, when the person needs to see the number while adjusting.
limits, when the ends of the scale are not obvious to the person.
marks, when only some values are valid, in fixed steps.
inputs, when the exact number matters and the person may want to type it.
steppers, when fine adjustment is common or dragging is hard, as on a touch screen.
Inside nph-field when the value breaks a rule: the field gives the error message.
do_not_use_when: To show progress: that is a progress bar, which is not operated.
range to pick a single value: use single.
vertical in a common form: the horizontal one follows the reading.
text inside nph-field: the label comes out twice.
limits together with marks: the marks already show the ends.
marks on a continuous scale: use limits.
Alone when the person often types exact numbers: turn on inputs or use nph-input.
steppers without a defined step: each click needs to move one clear step.

orientation.constraint: The vertical one serves a narrow panel; its minimum is at the bottom, and only text and limits exist in it. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the parts by it. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

mode.constraint: single picks one value with one thumb; range picks a start and an end with two thumbs. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the parts by it. Any other value draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

min.constraint: The lowest value of the scale. It must be below max; otherwise the slider draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

max.constraint: The highest value of the scale. When it is off the step, the slider stops at the last step below it.

step.constraint: The distance between two values the slider stops on. Every value is rounded to it. It must be a positive number; otherwise the slider draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

value.constraint: The current value, in single. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(), as in the native range: it applies only while the person has not moved the slider and setting the property has not made it dirty. Setting it from code fires no event.

start.constraint: The start of the range, in range, with the same rule as value. It never passes end.

end.constraint: The end of the range, in range, with the same rule as value. It never comes before start.

name.constraint: The name of the entry in the form data. single submits name=value; range submits two entries under the same name, start and end. Reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host.

text.constraint: The visible label, already localized, drawn by an nph-label with the current value beside it, above the track. Empty turns the part off. Off inside nph-field, which already gives the label.

limits.constraint: Turns on the minimum and the maximum at the ends of the track. Not together with marks.

marks.constraint: Turns on one label per step under the track, from min to max, at most 100. Horizontal only. In the vertical orientation, or above 100 steps, it is not drawn and emits console.error in development; the step does not change.

inputs.constraint: Turns on an nph-input with the number: one at the end in single, one at each end in range. The number is applied when the person presses Enter or leaves the field. Horizontal only.

steppers.constraint: Turns on the minus and plus buttons, which move one step. Horizontal only. Requires decrease-label and increase-label: without them, the buttons are not drawn and the slider emits console.error in development.

start-label.constraint: In range, the accessible name of the start thumb and of its field, already localized. Without it, the slider renders and warns in development.

end-label.constraint: In range, the accessible name of the end thumb and of its field, already localized. Without it, the slider renders and warns in development.

decrease-label.constraint: The accessible name of the minus button, already localized. Required with steppers.

increase-label.constraint: The accessible name of the plus button, already localized. Required with steppers.

label.constraint: The accessible name in text, never visible, for a slider with no associated label; nph-field writes it. An associated label wins over it, and it wins over text.

description.constraint: The accessible description in text, never visible: the help or the error sentence that nph-field writes. It is read as the description of each thumb.

required.constraint: Written by nph-field (P83). A slider always has a value, so it has no effect and is not announced.

disabled.constraint: The whole slider at state/disabled-opacity, once; the thumbs leave the Tab order and the form data. A disabled fieldset disables it too. It wins over invalid.

invalid.constraint: The error state: the thumb border becomes status/error and each thumb gets aria-invalid. The sentence belongs to nph-field; never invalid without it.

input.constraint: The native input event, while the value moves: at each key, click and drag step. It bubbles and crosses the shadow root. Read the value from the host.

change.constraint: The native change event, when the value settles: after a key or a click, and on the release of a drag that changed it. It bubbles. Setting a value from code fires neither event.

orientation.choose_when: horizontal in general use; vertical in a narrow panel or for a setting that goes up and down.
do_not_combine_with: vertical with marks, inputs or steppers.

mode.choose_when: single for one value; range for a start and an end.
do_not_combine_with: range to pick a single value.

parts.choose_when: text, limits, marks, inputs and steppers each turned on by a property, without creating a variant.

default.changes_for_user: The thumb at rest, with the color/primary-border border on color/background.

hover.changes_for_user: The value balloon opens above the thumb under the pointer.

focus.changes_for_user: The thumb border takes focus/border with the focus/halo outside, at focus/ring-width; the balloon opens.

error.changes_for_user: The thumb border is status/error; the inner fields show their error; the sentence is in nph-field.

error-focus.changes_for_user: The border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error; the balloon opens.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole slider at state/disabled-opacity, once; it does not respond, shows no balloon and wins over the error.

business_rules: Every value is rounded to the step and kept inside the scale, as the native range does.
In range, each thumb stops at the other.
A key, minus and plus fire input and change; a drag fires input at each value and change on release; setting a value from code fires nothing.
The field applies the number on Enter or when the person leaves it; a text that is not a number goes back to the value.
Minus and plus move the thumb used last, the start one by default (D2).
disabled wins over invalid: no error look on a slider the person cannot move.
domain_errors: invalid: the value breaks a rule; nph-field writes the sentence and passes it as description.

tokens.gap: space/stack-tight between the top line, the track and the marks; space/inline between the track and the parts beside it
tokens.track: color/input empty and color/primary active, space/inline-tight thick, radius/full
tokens.thumb: icon/size-sm, radius/full, color/background, border/width in color/primary-border

ai_hints: Use nph-slider when the position on the scale matters more than the exact number; when the exact number matters, turn on inputs or use nph-input.
Put nph-slider inside nph-field when it needs a help or an error message, and leave text off there.
Give a range slider start-label and end-label: each thumb has a name of its own.
Read value, or start and end, from the host on input or change; do not listen for an nph-* event.
Do not use it to show progress.

accessibility.semantics: Each thumb is an element with role=slider, with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext and aria-orientation; in range, an inner group holds the two thumbs. The host is form-associated and labelable.
accessibility.accessible_name: From the label associated with the host: nph-label for, a label element or nph-field. Without one, from label, then from text. In single, the name goes on the thumb; in range, on the group, and each thumb takes start-label or end-label. With no name, the slider renders and warns in development.
keyboard: Tab enters each thumb, then the field and the buttons.
The arrows move one step: Right and Up raise, Left and Down lower.
Page Up and Page Down move a tenth of the scale.
Home and End go to the ends; in range, to the other thumb.
accessibility.focus: The thumb shows the focus border and the halo on keyboard focus, and the balloon opens.
accessibility.contrast: The thumb border meets 3:1 against the background in both modes; the active part of the track is support. Support texts meet 4.5:1.
accessibility.color_alternative: The error is said by the sentence of nph-field, read as the description of each thumb; the current value is a number, in the balloon, in the label or in the field.

invalid_combinations: An orientation outside horizontal and vertical — the slider draws nothing.
A mode outside single and range — the slider draws nothing.
min not below max, or a step that is not a positive number — the slider draws nothing.
marks, inputs or steppers in the vertical orientation — the part is not drawn.
marks on a scale of more than 100 steps — the marks are not drawn.
steppers without decrease-label and increase-label — the buttons are not drawn.
limits with marks, and text inside nph-field — the slider renders and warns.
invalid without the sentence in nph-field — red with no text.
anti_patterns: Showing the error only through the thumb color.
Replacing the balloon with a fixed text above the thumb: use text.
Turning on limits together with marks.
Using marks on a continuous scale.
Using vertical in a common form.
